speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) what is the full cost of constructing and dismantling the temporary competition venue at Carpark G near the Kallang Tennis and Football Hubs for the 2025 World Aquatics Championships; and (b) what are the outcomes of any feasibility studies looking into extending the use of the competition venue after these Championships instead of dismantling it.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) what is the estimated number of international visitors expected to attend the 2025 World Aquatics Championships; (b) what methodology was used to arrive at this estimate; and (c) what is the projected total tourism revenue to be generated from these visitors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Family Development): Mr Speaker, with your permission, may I answer Question Nos 2 and 3 in today’s Order Paper, as well as the Parliamentary Question for oral answer filed by Mr Giam that is scheduled for a later Sitting, together, please?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The World Aquatics Championships (WCH) is the highest tier of world championships in aquatics.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: WCH 2025 will be the first time that an edition of the WCH is being held in Southeast Asia.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Global sports events such as WCH help Singapore to gain sporting prominence and mindshare internationally.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: As of January this year, our social media content on WCH 2025 has made more than 5.8 million impressions, across various platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, Tiktok, Weibo and XiaoHongShu.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: WCH strengthens Singapore’s reputation as a top-tier destination for international sporting events and reinforces our capabilities in hosting such large-scale events.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Beyond sports, the event will also have a related impact on tourism, hospitality and other industries, further raising Singapore’s profile as a travel destination.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The WCH 2025 will inspire local athletes and further encourage our population at large to participate in sports.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Our Team Singapore athletes can gain valuable experience from competing against the best athletes in the world and this in turn will bolster their chances of doing well at future tournaments.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Such opportunities to compete with the world’s best are significantly enhanced when world class competitions are held right here in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The WCH is not just for athletes but also for all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The event will rally Singaporeans together to cheer for Team Singapore in SG60, and we are confident that it will spark greater interest amongst Singaporeans for aquatic sports and inspire our next generation of sporting talents.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: This is a conservative estimate and comprises spectators and other visitors such as athletes, officials, production crew, media.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The final tourism receipts generated will be clearer after the event.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: For us to be able to host any large-scale sport competitions of the highest tier, we would have to put in place additional supporting infrastructure, as was the case for previous host cities of the WCH.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: For instance, the recent editions of WCH in Fukuoka and Doha required the construction of temporary pools to facilitate the hosting of the events at WCH, and coordination across the different aquatic events for officials, athletes and fans.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: For WCH 2025, with the OCBC Aquatic Centre hosting water polo and diving competitions, a temporary facility will be needed to host the swimming and artistic swimming competitions.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: If possible, this would further amortise the cost of staging the WCH.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: More details will be shared later as these require additional feasibility studies.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The construction cost of the temporary facility is being finalised, but it is expected to be comparable to that of other host cities which built temporary facilities to host the WCH.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: As host country, we aim to deliver a positive event experience for athletes and spectators alike, while being fiscally prudent and cost-effective.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The organising committee has been careful to reduce costs where possible, while working hard to secure sponsorships for these events.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: These sponsorships will help us defray some costs associated with operations and logistics of the event.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We have a sponsorship target and we are making good progress towards it.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We are in active discussions with various sponsors and we will reveal them progressively.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: At this point of time, we are unable to disclose details of the sponsorships due to commercial sensitivity.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The success of this event will depend on Singaporeans’ support.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, let us cherish this opportunity to show the world what we can do as a nation united and deliver a championships that we can and will be proud of.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Can I confirm that the temporary venue for this WCH event will remain up after the event, or will it be torn down?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I am mainly concerned about ensuring that the public resources put into constructing the temporary sporting venue are put to good use.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: My second question is, is the temporary sporting venue model expected to be a standard approach for hosting future large-scale sporting events in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: How does the Ministry ensure that the resources spent on such temporary infrastructure deliver long-term benefits, beyond a single event, to contribute to Singapore's sporting ecosystem, rather than simply fulfilling international bodies' hosting needs?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: More fine grain details of the masterplan are currently being worked through.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Various agencies like Sport Singapore, the Urban Redevelopment Authority for instance, will have to consider the various use cases of the plot for the mid to longer term.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: After considering sponsorships that we have garnered so far, I think it is reasonable for us to make a stand that we are more or less on track with this position.
